_doc: Tier-3 wilderness set piece for random worlds (site roadside: its front faces the road). Mostly outdoor: a fenced Cordon camp - prop fence sections, chain-link and white screens under razor wire, closing the compound; the chained gate; the checkpoint hut standing in the fence line is the only way through the wire. Inside: the screening tent and four ward tents are open-sided kit rooms (every edge an 'open' opening, a plank floor platform, open_roof) under w3_ward_tent props, so their sleepers stand in rooms; the decontamination line, the generator and three light towers (lit, generator-powered), a watchtower; the command trailer and the morgue reefer are kit rooms wearing shell props (w3_command_trailer_shell, w3_reefer_shell: their catalog entries mirror these rooms' sizes and openings) under style roof 'none'. Route: the road -> the checkpoint hut -> its inner door: the screening line turns -> the screening tent -> the decontamination line (jaws in the clothes) -> the wards -> the command trailer: the radio log, the captain's office behind a battery alarm, the reefer key (taking it wakes Ward B) -> the generator and the light towers -> the reefer, padlocked, a shotgun wired behind its door -> the morgue: Dr. Vance (guardian) and the cold-chain box -> the reefer's bolted side door, which opens beyond the wire (the reefer stands in the east fence line, so there is no way round the fence: the checkpoint is the way in). See docs/POI_AUTHORING.md.

defs.name: Cordon Quarantine Camp
defs.author: Hollowmere team (agent X)
defs.story: Site Q-4 was one of the Cordon Medical Authority's roadside camps: everyone coming down the road was screened at the gate. Under 38.0 went on the buses; over it went through decontamination to the ward tents, strapped to their cots, and stayed until the Medical Officer signed them out. Nobody was ever signed out. The dead went to the refrigerated trailer at the back, which was also where Dr. Imogen Vance kept the last forty-one doses of antifungal on cold chain, for the second wave of buses. There was no second wave. Captain Ruiz asked for extraction every night and was told to hold the site. The night the ground hummed every patient in the wards sat up at once; at two in the morning Sergeant Okoye opened the gate and walked into the trees, and at two-fifteen Ward B was up. The captain gave the doctor the reefer key and told her to go. She went to the reefer, rigged the corporal's shotgun behind its door, and lay down with the dead and the doses.
